fine_trace.note: The last 4 bytes of the fuzzer input are interpreted as a uint32 memory limit, controlling how much memory the custom allocator will permit.
The remaining input bytes are copied into a UA_ByteString that is passed to UA_Server_processBinaryMessage.
The raw input is parsed as a sequence of OPC UA TCP chunks; each chunk header (message type, chunk type, and chunk length) is validated against the connection's recvBufferSize.
With no secure channel attached, the chunk is decoded as a TcpMessageHeader; HEL and OPN are the only accepted message types.

fine_trace.code: case UA_MESSAGETYPE_HEL: retval = processHEL(server, connection, message, &offset);
fine_trace.note: A HEL message is processed, which sets the connection config (recvBufferSize, sendBufferSize, maxMessageSize, maxChunkCount) from the attacker-controlled HelloMessage fields.
The remote config from the HEL message is merged with the local config; recvBufferSize is capped at the local sendBufferSize (65535) and must be at least 8192.
An OPN message is decoded; the asymmetric security header (securityPolicyUri, senderCertificate, receiverCertificateThumbprint) is parsed from the chunk.
A new secure channel is created and attached to the connection; the channel's securityPolicy is selected based on the securityPolicyUri in the OPN header.
The OPN chunk is decoded as a SecureConversationMessageHeader; messageType, chunkType, and secureChannelId are extracted.
The asymmetric security header is decoded again from the OPN chunk; offset is set to UA_SECURE_CONVERSATION_MESSAGE_HEADER_LENGTH (12).
The chunk length is used as the initial size after decryption; this value is later used to compute the payload length.
The ciphertext region is defined from the offset to the end of the chunk; for OPN messages with security mode NONE, no actual decryption occurs.
For OPN messages, the signature size is obtained from the security policy's asymmetric crypto module.
The padding size byte is read from the chunk data at an index computed from chunkSizeAfterDecryption and sigsize; if the chunk is too small, this reads out of bounds.

fine_trace.code: if(offset + paddingSize + sigsize >= chunkSizeAfterDecryption) return UA_STATUSCODE_BADSECURITYCHECKSFAILED;
fine_trace.note: A bounds check is performed before signature verification; if the padding and signature sizes exceed the chunk size, the chunk is rejected.
The sequence header (sequenceNumber and requestId) is decoded from the chunk at the current offset.

fine_trace.code: payload->data = chunk->data + offset; payload->length = chunkSizeAfterDecryption - offset - sigsize - paddingSize;
fine_trace.note: The payload pointer and length are computed; the payload length is derived from chunkSizeAfterDecryption minus offset, sigsize, and paddingSize.
The payload is stored in the message's chunk payload list; the payload points into the original chunk buffer.
Complete messages are iterated; for a message with a single chunk payload, the callback is invoked directly with the payload bytes.

fine_trace.code: case UA_MESSAGETYPE_OPN: retval = processOPN(server, channel, requestId, message);
fine_trace.note: The OPN message is dispatched to processOPN, which decodes the OpenSecureChannelRequest from the payload.
The OpenSecureChannelRequest is decoded from the message payload; the request contains securityMode, requestedLifetime, and clientNonce.
The channel is opened with the attacker-controlled securityMode and a new channelId is assigned.
After the OPN is processed, any remaining complete messages in the channel queue are processed; a subsequent MSG chunk with the same requestId is appended to the same message.

For multi-chunk messages, a buffer of messageSize is allocated and the chunk payloads are copied into it; if messageSize is inconsistent with the actual payload lengths, this can cause a heap overflow.
The copy position advances by each chunk payload's length; if the sum of payload lengths exceeds the allocated messageSize, the memcpy writes past the end of the buffer.
